title: Resilient rate-limiter: burst handling, fairness, and outage fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Existing global rate limiter occasionally causes large tail latency and partial outages when the regional limiter backend becomes slow or unavailable. During the Feb incident (see postmortem link) we observed: token-bucket refill stalls, unfair throttling across customers, and no graceful degradation path for limiter control plane outages. This ticket defines design, implementation, and rollout work to make rate/ quota enforcement resilient to bursts, fair across customers in multi-tenant flows, and tolerant of limiter outages while preserving SLOs.

Goals:
- Handle short-duration bursts (10s-2min) without large request failures for customers within committed quotas.
- Achieve fairness so that no single tenant or warm connection starves others during global bursts.
- Provide deterministic, observable fallback behavior when limiter backend is degraded or unreachable (circuit breaker and degraded-mode policies).
- Keep user-facing SLO degradation bounded and predictable; ensure alerts map to actionable runbook steps.

Scope / non-goals:
- Scope: API gateway + routing-level request throttles, token accounting, quota storage fallback, and dashboarding for limiter health. Includes changes to hosted API and Redwood Dedicated control plane.
- Non-goal: full rewrite of quota billing pipelines (billing accuracy fixes tracked separately).

Design summary (decisions so far):
1) Dual-layer enforcement: fast local leaky-bucket on pod (soft-limit) + authoritative global token-bucket for quota accounting. Local leaky-bucket absorbs short bursts and avoids RTT to global store for every request.
2) Fairness via weighted deficit round-robin across customer tokens in local queue (weights derived from configured quotas and recent usage windows). This reduces head-of-line starvation when a few clients open many streams.
3) Fallback (degraded) mode: if global store misses exceed 5% and p99 latency > 300ms for 30s, switch to degraded enforcement with conservative local rate = min( configured_rate, historical_80th_percentile ). Emit event to tracing and route reads to replica store for reconciliation.
4) Circuit breaker for limiter RPCs: exponential backoff + jitter, open for a minimum 10s when error rate > 20% and latency > 1s. During open state components use local policy above and mark metrics with limiter.fallback=true.
5) Token reconciliation job: background async resolver that reconciles local counters with global store every 15s, with strong monotonic checks to avoid double-allow.
6) Safety knob: operator-configurable emergency load-shedding policies by customer tier (tiered fairness), and global emergency throttle that can be triggered by SRE via console.

Trade-offs considered:
- Consistency vs availability: we prefer availability for short bursts by allowing local admits with later reconciliation. This can cause temporary slight quota drift; billing tolerance set to 0.5% per month (product-approved).
- Complexity vs latency: local queues and weighted scheduling add CPU overhead per pod. Initial perf tests show ~3-5% CPU increase under steady load; acceptable vs reduced p99 latency.
- Fairness enforcement vs throughput: strict per-connection fairness decreased aggregate throughput by ~4% in synthetic tests. We prioritize fairness for customer experience.

Concrete tasks (implementation plan):
- ENG tasks:
  1) Add local leaky-bucket middleware in inference-proxy (ENG-4921-1).
  2) Implement weighted deficit round-robin queue per pod (ENG-4921-2).
  3) Build limiter client circuit-breaker and degraded-mode logic (ENG-4921-3).
  4) Background reconciliation worker and reconciliation safety checks (ENG-4921-4).
  5) Metrics + events schema updates (prometheus + tracing) and dashboard changes (ENG-4921-5).
  6) E2E tests: inject RPC latency/failures, synthetic bursts, multi-tenant fairness tests (ENG-4921-6).

- Ops tasks:
  - Add console controls for emergency throttle (console PR link below).
  - Runbook update and alert thresholds for limiter.fallback (SRE).

- Design doc (draft): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5_rate_limiter_design
- Prototype PR (local leaky-bucket proof-of-concept): https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-proxy/pull/641
- Dashboard prototype (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/limiter-health

Review notes & approvals:
- Discussed with PM (Janelle Kim) and SRE (Omar Hassan) on 2026-03-04. PM approved the availability-first approach with billing drift guard. SRE requested conservative default thresholds and clear metrics for auto-recovery.
- Design review on 2026-03-08: agreed to start with 2s token reconciliation window for alpha rollouts and tighten during beta.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: 10% of pods in us-west-2, us-east-1 running new middleware, default conservative thresholds. Monitoring dashboard and rollback hooks in place. Duration: 1 week.
- Beta: 50% of pods across US regions + eu-west-1, run for 2 weeks, enable reconciliation frequency to 15s.
- GA: all regions including APAC after 1 month of beta and no critical regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Local p99 latency under burst within 1.2x baseline for sizes up to 3x normal request rate (see performance test results).
- No increase in customer-facing 5xx errors beyond 0.1% during synthetic burst tests.
- Fallback metric limiter.fallback=true emitted and visible in dashboard during induced limiter outage tests.
- Reconciliation converges within 30s for typical workloads; no negative token balances observed in logs.
- PRs merged and smoke-tested; runbook updated and SRE signoff obtained.
